Love, Respect, Serve
Welcome to Lilliput Church of England Infant School
It is with immense pride that I welcome you to Lilliput CE Infant School as Headteacher.
I hope our website gives you a flavour of our thriving infant school, where our distinctly Christian identity and unwavering commitment to every child nurture the whole child and inspire a lifelong love of learning.
At the heart of everything we do are our core values of Love, Respect and Service. These values shape our relationships, guide our decisions and help us to create a community where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish.
We are incredibly fortunate to be situated on the beautiful Dorset coast, just a stone's throw from the golden sands of the Sandbanks Peninsula. Our school site is also bursting with life, with extensive wooded grounds providing a wonderful backdrop to everyday school life.
Our unique location enriches our curriculum, inspiring children to develop a sense of awe and wonder while encouraging them to care for the world around them. Through experiences both within and beyond the classroom, we aim to develop confident, compassionate young people who embody our values and make a positive difference to the lives of others.

pageCache.text:
Coastal Learning Partnership
Thank you for taking an interest in Lilliput CE Infant School, which is a highly valued member of the Multi Academy Trust, Coastal Learning Partnership (CLP).
CLP is a single family of sixteen schools across two Local Authority areas: Dorset Council and Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole Council. The two furthermost points of CLP are Boscombe and Swanage. There are about 5,400 pupils overall who are supported by around 900 committed staff.
Our schools work closely together in a spirit of professional generosity and collaboration, sharing resource and expertise.
Although part of the same single family, every school in CLP is different and unique and those differences are greatly valued. Each school has its own identify and values which express the local communities that they serve. Those schools within CLP which are church schools express their Christian distinctiveness through their unique vision.
CLP’s motto is ‘Broadening Horizons Together’. This is because we want every member of the CLP community to really flourish; children enjoy an inspiring educational experience and staff enjoy professional opportunity and fulfilment. That is achieved through being part of a single learning community.
CLP has three core values which influence the way in which we work together:
Serve: Schools in CLP serve each another as well as their local communities and families
Inspire: Staff inspire each other and their pupils
Empower: Schools, and everyone in them, are empowered to be their very best
Lilliput CE Infant School has made a commitment to the CLP family, secure in the knowledge that serving others in this way will lead to a better educational experience for all of the pupils.
If you would like to learn more about the work of CLP and its other schools, or to view documentation such as statutory accounts, please visit the Coastal Learning Partnership website here.

Inspection and Academic Results
Ofsted Report and Information
We are delighted to have received "good" in all main areas of our last OFSTED inspection in July 2023.
SIAMS Inspection
Our most recent SIAMS Inspection was held in school on 14th March 2019. We are delighted that we have been identified as an Excellent School. We have taken on board the areas for development highlighted and will be working on these improvements.
SIAMS is the Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools. This is also known as a Section 48 inspection. All church schools will undergo this inspection which is scheduled every five years. The new SIAMS judgments are: Excellent, Good, Requires Improvement or Ineffective.
SIAMS inspection focuses on the impact of the Church school's Christian vision on pupils and adults. This involves looking at the school’s Christian vision, the provision the school makes because of this vision and how effective this provision is in enabling all pupils to flourish. Church schools will employ a variety of strategies and styles appropriate to, and reflective of, their particular context in order to be distinctively and effectively Christian in their character and ethos. SIAMS inspectors therefore do not look for a set template of what a Church school should be like, but rather take the particular context of the school into account and base their evaluation on the outcomes rather than the process.
The Evaluation Schedule has one inspection question: how effective is the school’s distinctive Christian vision, established and promoted by leadership at all levels, in enabling pupils and adults to flourish?
This is explored through seven strands:
One overall grade is awarded reflecting the contribution of these strands to the flourishing of pupils and adults in a Church school. In addition a standalone grade is awarded in all schools for collective worship and in voluntary aided (VA) schools and former VA schools for religious education (RE). This grade is based on teaching and learning alone.
For more information about the processes, policies and protocols of SIAMS in your area please contact your local diocese.

Welcome from Headteacher
A very warm welcome to Lilliput CE Infant School.
It is a tremendous privilege to serve as Headteacher of this remarkable school and community. Lilliput is a place filled with joy, ambition, kindness and opportunity; a place where children are encouraged to flourish academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually.
We are fortunate to work with children during what I believe are the most magical years of education. The infant years are a time of wonder, curiosity and discovery, when lifelong attitudes towards learning begin to take shape. We take this responsibility seriously. Every day, we strive to create a school where children feel safe, valued and inspired, developing not only the knowledge and skills they need for future success, but also a genuine love of learning that will stay with them throughout their lives.
At Lilliput, we are unapologetically ambitious for every child. We know that a high-quality education has the power to transform life chances, open doors and create opportunities. Our curriculum is therefore rich, ambitious and academically rigorous, with high expectations for all. We want every child to leave us exceptionally well prepared for the next stage of their education and with the confidence to embrace the future.
At the same time, we are deeply committed to nurturing the whole child. Our distinctly Christian ethos lies at the heart of all we do, providing the foundation for a culture built upon our core values of Love, Respect and Service. These values shape our relationships, guide our decisions and help us to develop compassionate, thoughtful young people who understand their responsibilities to others and the positive contribution they can make to society.
We are blessed with a truly exceptional setting. Nestled close to the stunning Dorset coastline and surrounded by beautiful wooded grounds, our environment enriches our curriculum and provides endless opportunities for exploration and discovery. Children benefit from regular Forest School sessions throughout the year, as well as our popular after-school Forest School Club, helping them to develop resilience, independence, creativity and a deep appreciation of the natural world. Our unique location inspires a sense of awe and wonder and helps bring learning vividly to life.
What makes Lilliput especially special, however, is our people. We have a talented, dedicated and passionate staff team who work tirelessly to ensure every child thrives. Their commitment, care and belief in children are evident in every aspect of school life. We are proud of the strong partnerships we build with parents, carers, our local community and the Church of the Holy Angels, recognising that children achieve their best when we work together.
We are also committed to being approachable and accessible. The senior leadership team and I consider it a privilege to serve this school community, and we value the trust that families place in us. Whether you are considering Lilliput for your child or are already part of our school family, we look forward to building a strong relationship with you and supporting your child every step of the way.
Children love coming to Lilliput, and that is exactly how we believe school should be. It is an exceptional place to learn, grow and belong, and I am delighted to welcome you to our community.
Mr Lloyd B Allington Headteacher

Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium 2024 - 2027
To register your child for Pupil Premium please use this link.
At Lilliput Infant School, we believe that all children are entitled to an education which allows every child to achieve their potential regardless of their starting point in life or personal circumstances. The government believes that the additional funding provided for Pupil Premium children is the best way to tackle those inequalities to enable children to have the best outcomes.
Which pupils are entitled to Pupil Premium?
Pupil Premium Grant (PPG) is provided to all schools to support pupils within the following categories:
How do we encourage parents to register their child’s eligibility?
Registering is quick and easy by using this link. If you need any help, please speak to one of our office team or Mrs Chinchen. It will not affect any other benefits you are claiming and no families will know that you have registered.
What is Pupil Premium spent on?
The decision about how individual schools use their Pupil Premium is left to each school with the expectation that they will close the gap in attainment and progress between those eligible and other children nationally. “It is for schools to decide how the Pupil Premium is spent since they are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for the individual pupils within their responsibility.” (DfE). Therefore, schools are free to spend the PPG as they see fit. However, they will be held accountable for how they have used the additional funding to support these pupils.
In September 2023, EEF Guide to the Pupil Premium was updated and published by the Education Endowment Foundation. This supports schools in spending their Pupil Premium to maximise the benefit for their students. The report recommends schools take a tiered approach to Pupil Premium spending. Teaching should be the top priority, including professional development, training and support for early career teachers and recruitment and retention. Targeted support for struggling pupils should also be a key component of an effective Pupil Premium strategy; as well as strategies that relate to non-academic factors, including improving attendance, behaviour and social and emotional support. As a school we have used the information and research within this report to guide our spending of Pupil Premium money.
Government's Policy Paper on Pupil Premium - Updated February 2024
How is funding used at Lilliput Infant School?
At Lilliput, we use funding in a range of ways to support all pupils including those who qualify for Pupil Premium. In December 2024 we published our new three year plan which is a comprehensive strategy as to how we will support our pupils to meet their full potential. Class teachers and teaching assistants know which children are identified as pupil premium and, in termly pupil progress reviews, these children are a specific focus group. Throughout the academic year, we analyse the impact of any additional support, interventions and strategies used to ensure they provide best value and that progress is being made by these pupils.

PE and Sport Funding
Physical Education (PE) Curriculum
PE and sport are valued highly and play a very important part in the life of Lilliput C.E. Infant School. Therefore, as a staff team, we have carefully considered the units and skills we will teach based on our knowledge of how the children learn and what we believe will support the children at Lilliput most, in line with the EYFS framework and the National Curriculum. This is reassessed each year and is continually discussed throughout the year to allow children to receive a positive and strong experience of sport throughout their time at Lilliput.
Our teaching of each unit will be delivered incorporating our Christian Vision and Values. Equally, we will make our school's Key Skills for Life explicit to the children through our teaching and their learning.
Our Sports Role Model(s) of the half term is an exciting initiative that we champion at Lilliput. Each carefully selected role model relates to our half termly sports unit. They are introduced to the children during worship. The children have the opportunity to learn about each sports role model to appreciate their hard work, develop a deeper understanding towards each sports person and their sport. We hope to motivate, inspire and enhance the children's cultural capital through this endeavour.
Celebratory Sports Week
At the end of each unit, children at Lilliput experience a 'Celebratory Sports Week' where the children get the opportunity to apply the skills learnt during that unit of work to a team game, performance or tournament. During 'Celebratory Sports Week', a child from each class will also be awarded the 'Sports Person of the Half Term' in worship. 'Sports Person of the Half Term' will be awarded to children who have developed their skills and shown our school values in their PE lessons. These children are announced in our celebration worship and receive a special mention in our sports newsletter.
We encourage parents/ carers to share their child's sporting achievements outside of school with the PE Lead and class teacher. You can do this by emailing the school office. We will then share these achievements during 'Celebratory Sports Week' and, with your permission, in the sports newsletter.
At Lilliput C.E. Infant School, we are committed to the ongoing and sustained improvement of PE and sport. Our overall aim is to raise standards in PE and sport, increasing the participation and opportunities offered to our children. We aim to provide higher quality lessons and improved learning for all.
Since 2013, the government have been providing approximately £150 million per year to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in schools. The money must be used to improve the provision of PE and school sport. Ofsted continue to monitor the impact of this funding and schools have to account for how they have spent their Sport Premium money. Whole school intent, implementation and impact
At Lilliput CE Infant school, our aim is to provide our children with an ambitious, exciting and empowering curriculum that equips them for today and the future.
Our curriculum is designed to recognise children’s prior learning, provide first-hand experiences, allow children to develop independence as well as interpersonal skills, build resilience and become creative, critical thinkers ready for the next stage of their education.
We want all our children to have high expectations of themselves and to be able to apply their learning across a range of exciting learning experiences.
We build learning experiences into our curriculum that enable our children to see themselves as part of a wide and diverse world. Every child is recognised as a unique individual. We celebrate and welcome difference within our school community using our Christian vision of ‘Loving one another, respecting one another, serving one another’ to promote positive attitudes to learning. We ensure that community involvement is an integral part of our curriculum and invite visitors into school to enable the children to learn new skills and to share experiences.
Children leave Lilliput with a sense of belonging to an aspirational school community, where everyone is valued and successes are celebrated. Our focus on developing children’s moral, spiritual, social and cultural understanding gives purpose to the learning at Lilliput. We want our children to learn the key skills that will enable them to go on to make a positive contribution to their community and the wider society.
The whole school community shares a very strong sense of purpose and ambition. We embrace a pedagogy of a Growth Mindset approach. We expect all children to meet national expectations, to fulfil their early promise and to develop latent potential. High expectations of progress apply to all children, whether they are working above, at or below age-related expectations and includes children who have special educational needs.
We have an expectation of participation, fulfilment and success for all of our children.
Teaching and learning is characterised by ambitious objectives, proven teaching and learning strategies (explanation, modelling, scaffold, practise, regular retrieval practise), challenging personal targets, rapid and effective interventions to keep children on track and rigorous smart assessment to check and maintain pupil progress. Our subject leaders and teachers are highly skilled and their knowledge is continuously updated and regularly monitored by subject leaders and the senior leadership team.
Clear support plans are in place. Teachers offer higher levels of support for any children who experience any difficulties in maintaining progress or extra challenges to those who need it.
The impact of our curriculum model and teaching strategies will be continuously monitored, evaluated and adapted by subject leaders and the senior leadership team in order to ensure that children make at least expected progress against national expectations based on:

pageCache.text:
Open Days
We understand that choosing a school for your child is a really important decision for all parents and one of the best ways to get to know a school is to visit.
For children who are due to start Reception/ EYFS in September 2026, we have availability for parent/ carer tour sessions on the following days/times:
Thursday 27th November – 09.00. 10.00,
Tuesday 6th January - 09.00, 10.00, 11.00
If possible, we would ask that children do not accompany you on the parent/carer tours.
Please contact the School Office via email (Lilliput.Office@coastalpartnership.co.uk) to book on to your preferred session(s) for a parent/ carer tour.
We will confirm appointments via the email address you provide on the form closer to the day of your tour confirming details of the session.
We would request that you do not attend a session without a confirmed appointment.
In addition to the tours, we are also delighted to be able to share with you a virtual tour that we have filmed of the school’s provision so you can get an idea of what our school is like.
In addition, we have included some frequently asked questions so hopefully we have answered most of your queries. If not, please get in touch with us and we will be happy to help.
The Virtual tour has been created and directed by one of our former pupils - Annabelle Blackmore and we couldn't be prouder.
Enjoy our tour and thank you for taking the time to visit our website. We hope to see you soon.

Although part of the same single family, every school in CLP is different and unique and those differences are greatly valued. Each school has its own identify and values which express the local communities that they serve. Those schools within CLP which are church schools express their Christian distinctiveness through their unique vision.

PTA and Community Support
Helping Hands PTA
Please see our website for current news and events https://www.lilliputpta.co.uk/
For any more information about the PTA or any of the above please feel free to email us at lilliputinfantschoolpta@gmail.com.
You can find information regarding our accounts and annual returns on the Charities Commission website.
Fundraising
Help us to raise funds through Easy Fundraising by clicking here when buying online. A lot of on-line retailers are signed up for this scheme so please look to see if where you are buying from is there!
Fundraising through Co-Op
Helping Hands of Lilliput Infant School has been selected by Co-op to receive a share of its community fund. There are several charities in the area that will receive a share of the £18,000 up for grabs. If you already have a Co-Op card you can log into your account online and select us as your chosen charity. Once you have done this 1% of any money you spend on their own food and goods plus things like life cover will be donated to our fund pot.
If you do not have a Co-Op card it’s easy to join, for just £1 in store or online you can get a membership card and start earning money for our charity. This is such a great amount of money to earn for the school so please support it if you can!
Community Support and Services
There may be times when families need a little extra support - financial or emotional. You do not need to feel alone. There are many local organisations and support services that can help. School is also here to support in any way we can.
Holiday activities and food programme (HAF)
The holiday activities and food programme aims to help children receiving free school meals. For more information, visit the website.
Family Hubs and Outreach Centres
Across Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole there are six Family Hubs and three Outreach Centres (formerly called Children's Centres).
Hubs are based in central locations and cover a reach area to support all families that need Early Help services, ensuring that families get the right help at the right time. Any family can contact them and they will be able to signpost to appropriate support. For more information, visit the website.
Community Food Support
There are a number of different ways you can get food support including foodbanks, family hubs, and other community food settings which can be accessed through the ‘Access to Food Map’.
The access to food map is a tool to enable families to find where they will be able to access food support in the community and how to access support as well as providing information on community meals, cooked meal delivery, cooking workshops, foodbanks and social supermarkets.
To access this please visit the link below:
https://public.tableau.com/profile/bcpinsight#!/vizhome/AccesstoFoodMap/Introduction
Jimmy's Food Bank, Poole Quay and St Clements Church, Parkstone
Support for households in crisis with three-day emergency food parcels and a space for additional advice and support that tackle route issues of crisis. Referrals are available from frontline services (eg GP, citizens advice). For more information, visit the website.
Together We Can is an initiative led by BCP Council, working in close partnership with many other public, private and voluntary sector organisations. Families may be eligible for a food voucher if they are experiencing hardship and meet the two ‘Essential Criteria’ and one ‘Other Criteria’. Alongside this families might be eligible for financial support, support if you are clinically vulnerable or isolating, Mental health and wellbeing. For more information, visit https://www.bcpcouncil.gov.uk/News/News-Features/COVID-19/Help-advice-and-support/Help-advice-and-support.aspx
Please visit the link below if you would like financial advice, support with paying utility bills, advice for private rentals and much more.
https://www.bcpcouncil.gov.uk/News/News-Features/COVID-19/Help-advice-and-support/Financial-support/Financial-support.aspx
Lets Talk Money helpline with Citizens Advice
If you are currently struggling with your finances or are worried about managing your money, you can contact the Let's Talk Money team who can provide free help and guidance. Contact the team Monday to Friday from 10am - 4pm.
